Criterion: Verify the safety of the following: hook load, hold-down, and damping forces; off-center engagement capabilities; lateral run-outs; cable compatibility; deck and runway compatibility and any other specific engagement provisions. Standard: The arresting hook design minimizes the occurrence of the hook skipping over the cable and improves the ability of engaging the cable at the various cable and air vehicle positions (e.g., off center engagements, pitch, airframe dynamics at touchdown). Arrestments often cause violent hook and cable movements which can contact air frame structures. The system provides sufficient damping and protection to minimize any damage to the air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses, tests and demonstrations. Design analysis verifies compliance at all the specified arrestment conditions. Air vehicle demonstrations confirm the safe performance of the system in engaging the cable. Flight testing verifies the installation, functionality and performance capability of the arresting system to stop the air vehicle and to minimize air vehicle and cable damage. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.8.1.1, A.4.4.1.8.1.1 Air vehicle arrestment performance; through A.3.4.1.8.1.8, A.4.4.1.8.1.8 Hook actuation criteria MIL-A-18717 MIL-A-83136 (cancelled; for information only) AFGS-87139: 3.2.7.1 Arresting hook system SAE ARP1538

versions.title_at_revision: Arresting hook system's ability to engage the cable
versions.text:
Standard: The arrestment hook system engages the arresting cable and prevents damage to the air vehicle or stores. The arresting hook system design includes provisions which: a. Minimizes the arresting hook from contacting the runway or deck on landing in a direction that causes damaging compression loads to be developed in the hook shank and in the air vehicle structure. b. Minimizes the arresting hook point bouncing on landing impact, as the hook point drags along the landing surface, or hitting a runway/deck obstruction by incorporating damping to prevent a missed engagement. c. Takes into account cable dynamics due to tire rollover effects. d. Allows the hook to engage the cable with an air vehicle that has a flat nose tire and strut. e. Allows the hook to engage the cable under air vehicle dynamic bounce conditions. Hook point bounce that occurs during landing roll out, not caused by hook point contact with the runway/deck, but by the air vehicle’s compressed main landing gears rebounding as the nose gear compresses. f. Prevents collateral damage to the air vehicle due to a missed engagement, hook and cable from damaging the air vehicle after cable engagement due to cable dynamics, and hook slap due to a missed engagement. g. Allows lateral movement of arresting hook to conduct off-center (distance from runway/deck centerline) and multivariate (yaw, pitch and roll) engagements. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review installation drawings to verify arresting hook assembly can engage the cable/deck pendant at all air vehicle attitudes expected during carrier and field operations and aborted takeoffs. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct a dimensional and geometric analysis to verify the arresting hook system ability to engage the cable.
  (2) Conduct dynamic analysis or simulation of air vehicle and arresting gear system to ensure the arresting hook system can engage the cable. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct lab testing on damper to verify damping level minimizes hook bounce to prevent missed engagements. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Ground test: Conduct ground testing to verify the installation, functionality, and performance capability of the air vehicle arresting hook system to engage arresting gear systems (e.g., BAK- 12, Mark 7, AAG, and E-28).
    (3) Flight test: Conduct flight testing to verify the arresting hook system's ability to engage arresting gear system without damaging the air vehicle and arresting hook system.
